source_text: Καὶ τοὺς ἀπὸ τῶν Στωϊκῶν δὲ δογμάτων, ἐπειδὴ κἂν τὸν ἠθικὸν λόγον κόσμιοι γεγόνασιν, ὡς καὶ ἔν τισιν σι῾ ποιηταί, διὰ τὸ ἔμφυτον παντὶ γένει ἀνθρώπων σπέρμα τοῦ λόγου, μεμισῆσθαι καὶ πεφονεῦσθαι οἴδαμεν· Ἡράκλειτον μέν, ὡς προέφημεν, καὶ Μουσώνιον δὲ ἐν τοῖς καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἄλλους οἴδαμεν. Ὡς γὰρ ἐσημάναμεν, πάντας τοὺς κἂν ὁπωσδήποτε κατὰ λόγον βιοῦν σπουδάζοντας καὶ κακίαν φεύγειν μισεῖσθαι ἀεὶ ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες. Οὐδὲν δὲ θαυμαστόν, εἰ τοὺς οὐ κατὰ σπερματικοῦ λόγου μέρος, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὴν τοῦ παντὸς λόγου, ὅ ἐστι Χριστοῦ, γνῶσιν καὶ θεωρίαν πολὺ μᾶλλον μισεῖσθαι οἱ δαίμονες ἐλεγχόμενοι ἐνεργοῦσιν· οἳ τὴν ἀξίαν κόλασιν καὶ τιμωρίαν κομίσονται ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ ἐγκλεισθέντες. Εἰ γὰρ ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἤδη διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἡττῶνται, δίδαγμά ἐστι τῆς καὶ μελλούσης αὐτοῖς καὶ τοῖς λατρεύουσιν αὐτοῖς ἐσομένης ἐν πυρὶ αἰωνίῳ κολάσεως. Οὕτως καὶ γὰρ οἱ προφῆται πάντες προεκήρυξαν γενήσεσθαι, καὶ Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἡμέτερος διδάσκαλος ἐδίδαξε.
thought_title: Demons hate those who live by the Word
orientation: Justin is explaining to the Roman Senate why Christians are hated and persecuted, arguing that demons cause this hatred against all who live by reason.
pass_a_gloss: And those from the Stoic doctrines, since even in ethical teaching they have become orderly, as also in some things the poets, because of the implanted seed of the Word (Logos) in every race of humans, we know to have been hated and killed; Heraclitus indeed, as we said before, and Musonius in our times and others we know. For as we indicated, the demons always worked to make all those who in any way at all strive to live according to the Word and to flee wickedness to be hated. And it is no wonder if those who live not according to a part of the seed of the Word, but according to the knowledge and contemplation of the whole Word (Logos), which is Christ, the demons, being refuted, work to make them hated much more; who will receive the worthy punishment and penalty, being shut up in eternal fire. For if by humans already through the name of Jesus Christ they are defeated, it is a teaching of the punishment that is also going to be for them and for those who serve them in eternal fire. For thus also all the prophets proclaimed beforehand that it would happen, and Jesus our teacher taught.

choices.term: κἂν τὸν ἠθικὸν λόγον κόσμιοι γεγόνασιν
choices.english: since even in ethical teaching they have become orderly
choices.why: κἂν here means 'even in' with the accusative, and κόσμιοι means 'orderly' or 'well-behaved'; the clause gives the reason Stoics were hated despite their ethical virtue
rejected: even if they have become orderly in ethical teaching
though they became orderly in ethical teaching

choices.term: διὰ τὸ ἔμφυτον παντὶ γένει ἀνθρώπων σπέρμα τοῦ λόγου
choices.english: because of the implanted seed of the Word in every race of humans
choices.why: ἔμφυτον modifies σπέρμα and the dative παντὶ γένει ἀνθρώπων is locative; the phrase explains why Stoics and poets had ethical insight
rejected: because of the seed of the Word implanted in every race of humans

choices.term: οἳ τὴν ἀξίαν κόλασιν καὶ τιμωρίαν κομίσονται ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ ἐγκλεισθέντες
choices.english: who will receive the worthy punishment and penalty, being shut up in eternal fire
choices.why: The relative pronoun refers to the demons; the aorist passive participle ἐγκλεισθέντες is circumstantial, indicating the manner or condition of receiving punishment
rejected: who will receive the worthy punishment and penalty, having been shut up in eternal fire

pass_b_english: We also know that those who followed Stoic teachings have been hated and killed. They became orderly in their ethical life, as did some of the poets, because of the seed of the Word implanted in every race of humanity. Heraclitus, as I mentioned in my earlier defense, and Musonius in our own time, and others we know.
For as I have indicated, the demons have always worked to make hated everyone who strives in any way to live according to the Word and to flee wickedness.

And it is no wonder that the demons, being refuted, work much more to make hated those who live not according to a part of the seed of the Word, but according to the knowledge and contemplation of the whole Word, which is Christ. They will receive the worthy punishment and penalty, being shut up in eternal fire.
For if they are already defeated by human beings through the name of Jesus Christ, that is proof of the punishment that is also going to come upon them and upon those who serve them in eternal fire.
For thus all the prophets proclaimed beforehand that it would happen, and Jesus our teacher taught it.

problems.quote: that is a teaching of the punishment

problems.why: δίδαγμα means proof/token, not teaching; this changes Justin's argument structure.
problems.fix: that is proof of the punishment
problems.ruling: δίδαγμα here means proof/pledge/token, not 'teaching'; Justin argues present defeat proves future punishment.

last_rejected.why: English uses causative 'make hated' twice for passive 'μισεῖσθαι' (to be hated). This changes agency: demons cause hatred, not suffer it. But Greek says demons 'work to make hated' (ἐνήργησαν...μισεῖσθαι) with passive infinitive—actually the Greek does mean demons cause others to be hated. 'Make hated' is awkward but not wrong. Wait: 'μισεῖσθαι' is passive 'to be hated', and ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες takes this as result. So demons work so that [people] are hated. 'Make hated' is a fair rendering. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐνήργησαν...μισεῖσθαι: demons work so that people are hated; 'make hated' conveys causative sense adequately.

last_rejected.why: English 'those who serve them' renders τοῖς λατρεύουσιν αὐτοῖς. But check: the Greek says 'upon them and upon those who serve them'. English has 'upon them and upon those who serve them'. No omission. Wait—checking 'ἐσομένης ἐν πυρὶ αἰωνίῳ κολάσεως' = 'going to come...in eternal fire'. English has 'that is also going to come upon them...in eternal fire'. No omission.
last_rejected.ruling: τοῖς λατρεύουσιν αὐτοῖς rendered as 'those who serve them'; no omission in English text.

last_rejected.quote: work much more to make hated
last_rejected.why: English 'work much more to make hated' is awkward but conveys πολὺ μᾶλλον...ἐνεργοῦσιν. However, 'make hated' is repeated. The Greek has μισεῖσθαι (to be hated) as passive. The demons 'work' (ἐνεργοῦσιν) so that [these people] 'are hated much more'. The causative 'make hated' is not ideal but conveys the sense. Actually, re-reading: 'οἱ δαίμονες ἐλεγχόμενοι ἐνεργοῦσιν' = 'the demons, being refuted, work/are at work'. The object is 'πολὺ μᾶλλον μισεῖσθαι' = '[that they are] much more hated'. So 'work much more to make hated' slightly misrepresents the syntax but not the sense. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: πολὺ μᾶλλον μισεῖσθαι...ἐνεργοῦσιν: 'work much more to make hated' conveys sense despite awkward syntax.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'eternal fire' for αἰώνιον πῦρ. English uses 'eternal fire'—correct. 'Shut up in' for ἐγκλεισθέντες = 'shut in, enclosed, imprisoned'. 'Shut up in' is slightly colloquial but means 'confined in'. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐν αἰωνίῳ πυρὶ ἐγκλεισθέντες = 'shut up in eternal fire'; standard rendering, no meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: They will receive the worthy punishment and penalty
last_rejected.source_quote: οἳ τὴν ἀξίαν κόλασιν καὶ τιμωρίαν κομίσονται
last_rejected.why: English 'They will receive the worthy punishment and penalty'—but οἳ refers back to οἱ δαίμονες (the demons). The preceding clause ends with 'the demons...work much more to make hated those who...' Then οἳ = 'who' referring to demons? Actually, grammatically οἳ could refer to demons or to the people. Contextually, it must be the demons who receive punishment. But the English 'They' without clear antecedent is ambiguous. However, context makes it clear. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: οἳ refers to δαίμονες; 'They' is contextually clear as demons receiving punishment.

last_rejected.quote: For thus all the prophets proclaimed beforehand that it would happen
last_rejected.source_quote: Οὕτως καὶ γὰρ οἱ προφῆται πάντες προεκήρυξαν γενήσεσθαι
last_rejected.why: English 'proclaimed beforehand that it would happen' for προεκήρυξαν γενήσεσθαι. The 'it' refers to the punishment in eternal fire. 'Thus' for οὕτως. 'For thus' for Οὕτως καὶ γὰρ—English splits this. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Οὕτως καὶ γὰρ...προεκήρυξαν γενήσεσθαι: 'For thus...proclaimed beforehand that it would happen' is accurate.

last_rejected.why: English 'taught it' adds 'it' not in Greek. Greek simply says 'Jesus our teacher taught'. The 'it' refers to what was proclaimed. This is a minor addition for natural English. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐδίδαξε: adding 'it' is natural English ellipsis resolution, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: work much more to make hated those
last_rejected.why: 'work to make hated' is awkward English. A modern reader can follow it, but it's strained. However, the instruction says not to report style preferences. This is borderline unreadable but technically comprehensible. No error.
last_rejected.ruling: Awkward style, not a major error; meaning is comprehensible per instructions.
